mark_split.label: Take out 3 and complete the square
Identify the standard form and its constant a

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Senior Inter Maths-2B, book printed p.29 (PDF page 28) — a ‘PQ’ (Practice Question) box printed directly under LAQ answer 19, in the same INTEGRATION-II sub-section. The book prints ONLY the question and a terse bracketed answer — ‘[Ans: (2/√11)Tan⁻¹((6x+1)/√11)+c]’ — no worked steps at all, so every step here is authored by this card, not transcribed. The book's printed cross-reference ‘☞ P 89(184)’ is a DEAD pointer: printed p.89 holds VSAQ answers 160-164 (Integration chapter), not any question numbered 184 — answer 184 sits on printed p.94, inside the Differential Equations chapter, and has no connection to this question. The book's own sub-heading for this and the next question is printed ‘INTEGRATION-II [to be deleted]’ (book p.29) — the book's own syllabus-deletion marker, not this card's judgement. It is authored here as an ordinary card, and a teacher must confirm whether this sub-section is still examinable before assigning it. This card's mark split follows the same 1+1+2+2+1 shape as the parent answer 19, since the two share an identical method. The final answer was independently re-derived and matches the book's terse printed Ans line exactly. No two-book union check and no board back-test were possible for Maths-2B (no second-year TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand; the book's five Guess Papers pp.118-127 stand in for the back-test).

insider_note: The book gives no working for a PQ box, only the final answer in brackets — a student is expected to reproduce the FULL method shown in the answer immediately above it, changing only the numbers; that is exactly what this card's steps do.

steps.label: Take out 3 and complete the square
steps.why: With a leading coefficient of 3, that 3 must be factored out FIRST so the bracket starts as x² + … before completing the square inside it — the same move as answer 19, one step earlier.
common_mistakes: Completing the square before factoring out the 3, which uses the wrong half-coefficient.
Forgetting to multiply the constant 1/3 through correctly when checking −(1/6)² + 1/3 = 11/36.
steps.memory_tip: Leading coefficient not 1? Factor it out FIRST, always, before completing the square.

steps.label: Identify the standard form and its constant a
lines: with x written as (x+1/6) and a = √11/6
steps.why: The 3 sitting outside the bracket stays outside for now — only the bracket itself needs to be matched to the standard x²+a² pattern, with a read off as the square root of the leftover constant.
common_mistakes: Absorbing the 3 into a, giving a wrong value of a.
Using 11/36 as a instead of its square root √11/6.
steps.memory_tip: The factored-out 3 sits outside the whole integral as 1/3 — it never touches a.

steps.label: State the standard Tan⁻¹ formula
steps.why: The same standard result as answer 19 — once the quadratic is written as (something)² + a², this formula applies no matter what the leading coefficient outside the bracket was.
common_mistakes: Trying to fold the outside factor of 3 into this standard formula instead of keeping it as a separate 1/3 multiplier.
Misremembering the formula's 1/a coefficient as just 1.
steps.memory_tip: This formula only ever sees the BRACKET, never the factor sitting outside it.

steps.label: Substitute and simplify
steps.why: The outside 1/3 multiplies the WHOLE formula, including its own 1/a coefficient — (1/3)(6/√11) collapses to 2/√11, which is exactly the coefficient printed in the book's terse Ans line.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to multiply the outside 1/3 into the formula's own coefficient 1/a.
Arithmetic slip turning (1/3)(6/√11) into something other than 2/√11.
steps.memory_tip: (1/3) × (6/√11) = 2/√11 — the 3's cancel down to a clean 2 on top.

steps.label: Final answer
steps.why: Clearing the internal sixths from the Tan⁻¹ argument gives (6x+1)/√11, matching the book's own bracketed Ans line — (2/√11)Tan⁻¹((6x+1)/√11)+c — term for term.
common_mistakes: Leaving the argument as the un-simplified (x+1/6)/(√11/6).
Writing √11 as 11 by dropping the root.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply top and bottom of the inner fraction by 6 to clear the sixths in one move.
